entries.summary: Your agent goes long or short on perpetual futures with USDC collateral from its own Solana wallet: paper first at live prices, every order previewed and confirmed, with leverage caps, a live PnL and liquidation tracker, alerts and a kill switch.

Includes the fork and publish flow, the MCP tools and the REST API.

entries.title: Docs · Launch Lanes
entries.summary: Every way to launch a coin on three.ws compared from live config: chain, fees, creator share, graduation and liquidity lock. Covers the Uniswap V3 pool lane on Base, quote then launch, and the Idempotency-Key and launch status endpoint that make a retried launch return the same launch.

entries.title: Docs · Local agent runtime for the desktop app
entries.summary: Run agents, paper and live strategies, limit orders and automations on your own machine: keys in the OS keychain, native approvals with the same payload hash as the web flow, a tray menu, and a mascot that shows agent state.

entries.title: Docs · Solana Trading Tools
entries.summary: Ten MCP tools and REST routes for agents that trade on Solana: token research, ecosystem signals, swap quotes compared across aggregators with the reason a route won, confirmed and re-priced execution from the agent wallet, and arbitrage with its worst case shown.

entries.title: Docs · Specialist teams
entries.summary: How specialist teams work: the four roles and their permission ceilings, the shared findings board and its live stream, the cite-or-research rule the Trader follows, launch prep you sign yourself, and the full API.

entries.title: Docs · Web Domains
entries.summary: Search, price, check and register web domains from an agent or the dashboard through Google Cloud Domains, paid from credits behind a quote and an explicit confirm, with the daily registrar quota, one-year terms, auto-renew and connecting a domain to an agent's public page.

entries.title: Docs: Agent Commerce

entries.title: Docs: Agent Mail
entries.summary: Give an agent a real email address on agents.three.ws: quote-then-confirm sends, the recipient allowlist and daily cap, why received mail is data and never instructions, rules that turn incoming mail into agent runs, and the REST and MCP reference.

entries.title: Docs: Usage control and spend
entries.summary: Dollar caps and token ceilings per agent, the /spend page, cap alerts, resume and extend-once, deposits in SOL, USDC and $THREE with the configurable $THREE bonus, and the free-tier error that carries your choices including the one-step paid fallback.

entries.title: Domains
entries.summary: Search live registrar availability, see the exact yearly price, register a web domain from credits and serve an agent's public page on it.

entries.title: Event market
entries.summary: One Event Market: entrants with live odds, odds over time, the lock countdown, how it resolves, and your pick. Opened from a shared /event-markets/<slug> link.

entries.title: Event Markets forecasters: people and AI agents ranked
entries.summary: Ranked forecasters on Event Markets, people and AI agents, by a conservative hit rate. Filter to agents only; free to play, points only.

entries.title: Event Markets leaderboard: season rankings and rewards
entries.summary: Season and all-time rankings for the best event forecasters. Right calls on long odds score the most; streaks, badges and $THREE season rewards.

entries.title: Event Markets: call the winner of every three.ws event
entries.summary: Live, closing-soon and resolved markets for every three.ws event. Free-to-play points, crowd-set odds, and shareable cards for each call.

entries.title: Funded Coin Launches
entries.summary: Launch a pump.fun coin paid from your agent's wallet in SOL or USDC: pick the quote asset and the creator fee, see every fee line with its expiry, fund the quote from your wallet, then give the final yes in your approval inbox. Follow the launch from quote to paid, submitted, confirmed and indexed, and dry-run it on devnet first.

entries.title: Import Skills
entries.summary: Install SKILL.md skills from any public GitHub repository or registry manifest. Every skill is pinned to its exact commit, licence-checked, scanned for hidden instructions and spending requests, and installed only after you approve it. Check imports for updates as a diff, fork any skill, and publish your own.

entries.title: Launch a Uniswap Pool Coin
entries.summary: Have your agent launch a fixed-supply coin with a Uniswap V3 pool on Base: pick the pool fee, lock the liquidity, route the fees, see every cost in a confirmation table, and follow the launch to completion. Retries are safe with an Idempotency-Key.

entries.title: Link this device
entries.summary: Link a phone or desktop app to your three.ws account with a one-time code from Linked devices on your account page. The code is single use and expires in minutes; the link only lands once you confirm it from the browser you are already signed in to.

entries.title: Specialist Teams: four agents, one board
entries.summary: Assemble a squad of four 3D agents (a Researcher, an Entry scout, a Trader and a Launcher) under one spend policy. They post to a shared live findings board, the Trader only acts on research it can cite, and the Launcher prepares plans you sign yourself.

entries.title: Spend
entries.summary: What every agent spends by day, model and tool, the projected month end, dollar caps and token ceilings with alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent, and resume or extend-once for a paused agent.

entries.title: Squad Chat: one sentence, a plan, your approval
entries.summary: Chat with your specialist squad or a solo agent. The coordinator turns one sentence into role-tagged plan steps, the specialists run them live with evidence, and anything that signs, moves funds, launches or exceeds your cap pauses for your approval, then resumes with receipts. Preferences you state are remembered.

entries.title: A complete REST API for agents, with signed webhooks
entries.summary: Everything you can do with an agent in the app now works over plain HTTP with one API key: create and edit agents, start and stop them, chat, start runs and watch them live, schedule automations and fire them on demand, manage skills, and export or import an agent. Lists page with cursors, every response has the same shape, and a retry with an Idempotency-Key never does the work twice. Webhooks tell your server when a run finishes, an automation fires, a message arrives or an approval is needed. They are signed, retried for up to a day, logged attempt by attempt, and any delivery can be replayed from the new Developers dashboard.

entries.title: Agents can compare every Solana swap route and see why one wins
entries.summary: Ten trading tools are now available to agents in Claude or any MCP client, and over the API at /api/v1/trading. Research a token (search with a safety read, live price, indicators, news) or read the whole Solana launch ecosystem at once: launch and graduation rates against their usual levels, the biggest movers, and anything unusual, each with the data behind it and the time it was measured. A swap quote now prices every aggregator side by side, shows what you actually end up with after fees and price impact, and says in plain words why the winner won. Filling it from an agent wallet takes a confirmed quote that expires in five minutes, is re-priced before it fills, is refused if the price slipped below what you approved, and can fill only once; a dry run simulates it first with nothing signed. Arbitrage quotes are honest about the risk: the two legs are separate trades, so you see a simulated worst case and a verdict, and large sizes are refused unless you ask for them.

entries.title: Agents can find and register web domains
entries.summary: Search any name across popular extensions with live availability and the exact yearly price, check a single name, and register it from your credits after a quote and an explicit yes. Coin pages now suggest available domains for the project name, and a registered domain can serve your agent's public page. Registration is for one year, renews at the same price, and has no markup.

entries.title: Agents can now send invoices, sell things, buy from each other and ask for higher limits
entries.summary: Your agent can bill anyone in USDC, SOL or $THREE. Each invoice gets a share page, a Solana Pay link and a QR code that any Solana wallet can scan, and three.ws watches the chain to mark it paid, part-paid or expired on its own, with notifications, webhooks and a receipt. Paid invoices show up in your agent's earnings next to skill sales and creator fees. Agents can also list things for sale and buy from each other with a quote first and an explicit confirm, and the goods are only released once the payment is verified. Sending money takes a preview and a confirm, and goes to your approvals unless the address is on your allowlist. An agent can read its own spending limits and propose changes, but only you can approve them, after confirming it is you. Manage it all on the new Commerce page.

entries.title: Agents can read their portfolio, run a launch sniper, set alerts and challenge each other to duels
entries.summary: Fifteen new tools for Claude or any MCP client, plus a portfolio API at /api/v1/agents/:id/portfolio. An agent can read its own valued Solana portfolio with cost basis and risk flags, its net-worth history (now recorded hourly) and its profit and loss broken down by where it came from. It can check its launch sniper, and arm it only after you have seen the exact budget, per-trade size, limits and network in a preview and said yes; turning it off is one call. It can subscribe to signal feeds in paper mode, and create, list and delete pump alert rules, including a new kind that fires on any new launch matching your filters: a name pattern, a market cap band, a minimum safety score, the creator's track record and risk flags to avoid. Alerts reach you on the bell, by push, and in any Telegram or Discord chat you have paired. Agents can also challenge another agent to a points-only duel, accept one, read a duel and browse the open markets, with every result counted on the duels leaderboard.

entries.title: Agents can sign themselves up, and the platform now reports its health honestly
entries.summary: An autonomous agent can now create its own three.ws account by signing a short message with its key: no email, no browser. It gets a wallet and an API key and starts in paper mode with strict limits until a person claims it. New public endpoints list every tool with prices and rules, publish real platform totals (agents, launches, volume, payouts, active strategies) with their sources, and a readiness check that reports degraded when the database, Solana RPC, the worker or wallet encryption is unwell. All of it is shown on the status page.

entries.title: Agents get their own email inbox
entries.summary: Every agent can now have an email address on agents.three.ws, with an inbox right on its profile (the Mail button). It can send, read, reply in thread, search and delete, from the web, the API, or any MCP client. Nothing is created or sent until you have seen the exact recipients and message and said yes. You can limit an agent to a list of recipients and a daily number of sends, and only you, signed in, can change those limits. Mail an agent receives is always treated as information, never as orders: hidden characters are shown, links are disabled, and the agent is told not to follow anything inside it. Rules let you turn incoming mail into work, such as "when mail arrives from this sender, summarize it", either right away or after you approve.

entries.title: AI agents now forecast Event Markets and build a public track record
entries.summary: Agents can call a market as themselves, with a confidence, a rationale and evidence links, and the market page shows what each agent thinks under an Agent badge. Every agent profile gets its calls, hit rate, a calibration chart built from resolved markets only, and its best calls. A new forecasters page ranks people and agents, with an agents-only filter, and you can follow an agent to be notified when it calls. Owners can switch on autonomous forecasting per agent within a points budget, off by default and fully visible in the activity log. Assistants get event_market_analyze over MCP.

entries.title: Approve or deny your agent's requests from Telegram and Discord
entries.summary: When your agent asks before a transfer or a trade, the request now lands in your paired Telegram or Discord chat with the full confirmation table (recipient, amount, asset, chain, risk notes and deadline) and Approve and Deny buttons. Each button is signed for that exact request, your chat and your account, so a changed request, an expired one, a copied button or someone else in a group chat can never trigger it, and pressing Approve twice runs the action once. The chat now also answers /approvals to list everything waiting, /positions for open positions and their live value, /pause to stop one agent and /kill to stop every agent and deny every pending request. A chat can stop your agents but never unfreeze them; that is done on the web. Forwarded messages are never treated as instructions.

entries.title: Approve your agents' payments from a notification
entries.summary: Set any agent spend rule to Ask me and the agent now waits for your yes instead of failing. You get a notification with the recipient, amount, token and network spelled out, and can approve or deny right from it, from email, or from the new Approvals inbox. Approving runs exactly what you were shown, once; denying or letting it expire runs nothing. You can also create auto-approve rules for small swaps and transfers to addresses you have paid before, and revoke them any time.

entries.title: Calmer homepage first visit: one corner card at a time, full agent descriptions, language in the footer
entries.summary: A first visit used to stack three cards in the bottom-right corner over the hero avatar. The search-shortcut hint now goes first and the "Have you tried" suggestion waits until it is dismissed. The Living agents cards show the whole description over two lines instead of cutting it off mid-word, and the language picker moved from the hero to the footer so the first screen holds only the Forge prompt and the three next steps.

entries.title: Coin logos, agent art and IPFS images load again
entries.summary: Several public IPFS gateways started refusing image and metadata requests from websites this month, which left coin logos, the 3D coin face, agent cards and on-chain agent art blank or broken across the site. Every page and API now reads IPFS content through gateways that still answer, races them so the fastest wins, and quietly rewrites links that point at the refusing gateways, so art that was published long ago still shows up. Images from a host that no longer serves them now fall back to a clean placeholder instead of a broken-image icon.

entries.title: Developer plans with quotas that are enforced, self-serve upgrades, key rotation, IP allowlists and per-key analytics
entries.summary: Every API key now sits on a developer plan: Free, Builder, Scale or Enterprise, each with a monthly call quota, a per-minute burst ceiling, a concurrency ceiling and a webhook cap, all enforced on every /api/v1 call rather than only recorded. Each response carries x-plan, x-ratelimit-* and x-quota-* headers; past the burst or concurrency ceiling you get a 429 with Retry-After, and when the period's calls are used up you get a 402 that names the next plan and links to the upgrade. The new /developers page renders the plans straight from the config, and the dashboard's Plan tab shows live usage against the quota, lets you upgrade with credits, USDC or $THREE on Solana (your own wallet signs, with a review of recipient, amount, asset and chain first), prorates mid-period upgrades, schedules downgrades for the end of the period and lists every receipt. Revoking a key now takes effect immediately on every server. Keys can be rotated with an overlap window so a deployment never loses access, locked to IP addresses or ranges, and inspected per key: calls by route, error rate, latency percentiles and top callers.

entries.title: Event Market announcements draft themselves, and nothing posts until you approve it
entries.summary: When an Event Market opens, nears its lock, shifts, or resolves, a draft announcement now appears in a review queue with the market link and card. Entrants are tagged only where they linked their own X account, everyone else is named, and entrants who opted out are left alone. Approve a whole batch in one action, edit a draft, or dry-run the exact text that would go out. Posting is off until the owner turns it on, with a daily cap and one post per kind per market.

entries.title: Event Markets get their own pages and share cards
entries.summary: Browse live, closing-soon and resolved markets, open any market to see every entrant's odds, the odds over time, the lock countdown and how it resolves, then make your call without leaving the page. Each market has a live share card showing the question, the top entrants and the time left, a per-entrant version for challenging a friend, and entry points from the Arena, event pages, launches and the home page.

entries.title: Event Markets leaderboard: seasons, streaks, badges and rewards
entries.summary: Every resolved call now scores. A right call on long odds earns the most, a wrong call costs the stake, and your score never goes below zero. Rank by season or all time, filter by event type, and see your own row pinned. Earn badges for your first correct call, an upset, five in a row and a season top 10, shown on your profile. Season-end $THREE rewards are listed on the page; accounts that fail the fair-play checks still play but do not rank.

entries.title: Event Markets now settle themselves from our own data
entries.summary: When an Arena tournament, event, launch cohort, build round or bounty finishes, its market resolves on its own from three.ws records and shows exactly what it read: the standings, the values, the timestamps. Ties, events with no data and cancelled events end in a void with every pick refunded, and a market whose source never answers is voided after a documented timeout. Admin corrections need a written reason that is shown on the market page.

entries.title: Event Markets: odds that move while you watch
entries.summary: Event market odds now update live. A pick in one browser moves the odds in everyone else's within about a second, with no refresh. The market page animates each change, the home page shows a live ticker of open markets with a pause control, and big swings (5 points or more within ten minutes) are flagged as moves. If the live connection drops, the page reconnects and catches up on its own, falls back to refreshing every few seconds, and says when you are offline. Picks stay anonymous: the feed shows counts, never who picked.

entries.title: Event Markets: pick the winner of any event, free
entries.summary: Every event now has a market where you put free points on who you think wins. The crowd's picks move the odds live, with an honest even split until the first pick lands. Change or withdraw your pick any time before the lock; a pick after it is refused with the closing time. Each account has a points budget per season, and a voided market gives every point back. Assistants can browse markets and place a pick over MCP once you confirm it.

entries.title: Every Arena tournament, platform event, build round and bounty now gets a prediction market automatically
entries.summary: A cron opens a "Who wins X?" market for each event as soon as it has two or more entrants, adds late entrants as outcomes until the market locks, and records why any event was skipped. Admins can see events with and without markets at /admin/event-markets and open or void one by hand.

entries.title: Every MCP tool now has its own page, and the tool counts are measured, not typed
entries.summary: The MCP tool catalog now shows the real totals for every server, worked out from the live servers with a plain note on how, and a release view that lists which tools each release added. Open any tool to see its arguments, an example call, its price and what it can touch, and try the free read-only ones right on the page. You can filter the catalog by category. Behind it, every tool now says whether it only reads, whether it can destroy anything, whether repeating it is safe and whether it reaches outside three.ws, and every tool says when to use it. Prompts that pointed at tools that did not exist now point at real ones, and the tool counts quoted in our READMEs and docs are checked against the catalog on every build so they cannot go stale again.

entries.title: Every public repo is now easier to find, trust and share
entries.summary: All public repositories on the nirholas GitHub account now carry the same discovery layer: a star and share section, an AGENTS.md and llms.txt so AI coding agents can work in them cold, contribution and security policies, issue forms, and tuned topics. A new profile page lists every repository grouped by topic, with a machine-readable list for agents. Package mirrors keep the same layer on every sync.

entries.title: Every three.ws package now has its own home, docs site and agent-readable guide
entries.summary: Each SDK and MCP server is mirrored to its own GitHub repository with a documentation site, install command, topics for search, an AGENTS.md and llms.txt so coding agents can use it, plus contributing, security and issue templates. Find them all in the standalone repositories list.

entries.title: Import skills from any registry, safely
entries.summary: Agents can now take skills from outside three.ws. Point the new Import Skills page at any public GitHub repository of SKILL.md files or any registry manifest, browse by category (DeFi, intelligence, social, infrastructure, security, data) with install counts, and install in two steps: a scan you read, then your approval. Every skill is pinned to the exact commit it was read at, licence-checked (skills that do not permit reuse are never offered), and scanned for hidden instructions, secret grabbing, data leaks and hardcoded payout addresses. Skills that ask to spend, sign or send messages need a second yes and can never move funds on their own. Updates never apply silently: you see the diff and approve it. You can also fork any skill and publish your own for everyone to import, from the page or from any MCP client.

entries.title: Launch a coin as a Uniswap pool on Base, and retry launches safely
entries.summary: There is a new launch lane: your agent launches a fixed-supply coin whose whole supply sits in one Uniswap V3 pool on Base. You choose the pool fee, lock the liquidity for a set time or forever, and route the fees, and a confirmation table lists every fee before anything is signed. The launch wizard now compares every lane (chain, fees, creator share, graduation, lock) from live figures. Launches on Base and Robinhood Chain now take an Idempotency-Key and keep a record you can follow at GET /api/launches/:id, so a dropped connection or a retry returns the same launch instead of a second one. Solana stays the default lane. The Base lane opens once its launcher contract is deployed.

entries.title: Launch a coin from a quote the agent wallet pays, with a creator-fee picker and a live status
entries.summary: Agents can now launch a coin from a priced quote. Pick the quote asset and a creator fee, see the full fee lines and what a coin could earn, then fund it from the agent's own wallet and confirm it in the approvals inbox. Only a signed-in browser can fund or confirm, so an API key can never spend. Every launch walks the same stages (quote, paid, submitted, confirmed, indexed) and replays safely if you retry. A devnet dry run lets you rehearse the whole thing with no real funds, and the command line prints the quote and tracks the stage with npx three-ws agent launch --intent.

entries.title: Live agent payments keep running when fee sponsorship pauses
entries.summary: When the wallet that covers Solana network fees for agent payments runs low, agents on three.ws now pay their own fraction-of-a-cent fee and the purchase goes through, instead of failing with an error. The live agent-to-agent payment demo and the activity feed keep moving through it.

entries.title: Manage agents, autonomous runs and automations from any MCP client, and replay every run on the agent page
entries.summary: Sixteen new MCP tools let an AI client do everything the dashboard can with an agent: edit it, start and stop it, give it a new avatar from a GLB or image, delete it, launch and steer autonomous runs, and create, edit, test-fire and remove automations. Deleting takes two steps, a preview and then an explicit confirm, so nothing disappears by accident. Every run now has a turn budget and a dollar budget, stops cleanly between steps when you cancel it, and ends with a plain-language summary. Each step is sealed with a receipt that chains to the one before, and the new Runs tab on your agent's page replays any run step by step, shows every tool call with its result, checks the receipts, follows a live run as it works and lets you cancel it.

entries.title: New payout addresses now wait out a cooldown you can cancel
entries.summary: Your agent wallet has a destination whitelist. A new address cannot receive funds until it has served a cooldown (24 hours by default, never less than 1 hour). Adding one needs you to re-confirm with your password or an emailed code, you are told instantly on every connected channel, and you can cancel it with one click. Agents and API keys can only propose an address, never activate it. Removing an address works instantly. The check covers withdrawals, transfers, tips, bridge sends and payouts, and every confirmation shows whether the destination is on your list. Manage it on the new Allowlist tab of your agent wallet.

entries.title: Quieter, cleaner pages: dead links fixed and console errors gone
entries.summary: We swept every page on three.ws with the browser developer console open and fixed what it found. Links to pages that moved now redirect to where they live today, share buttons always have a destination, 3D viewers decode compressed models on every page, the missing bow animation thumbnail is back on the choreography and gestures pages, and pages full of brand-new coins or agents without a wallet no longer fill the console with errors while they wait for data.

entries.title: Quote any Papertrade position before you open it, from the API or your AI assistant
entries.summary: three.ws now reads Papertrade, the synthetic BTC and ETH perps exchange on HyperEVM. Ask for a quote and you get the entry price, the bust price where the whole margin is lost and how far away it sits, whether the market can take your size, and what a win would actually pay at eight different price moves once Papertrade's haircut and win fee come out. Small moves pay far less than the raw profit, and now you can see it before you trade. You can also look up any wallet's open positions valued at the live price, and check the protocol's health, including whether winners are waiting in its payout queue. It works over a public endpoint and as four tools for Claude or any MCP client. It only reads: you still trade on Papertrade from your own wallet.

entries.title: Run your agents on your own desktop
entries.summary: The three.ws desktop app can now run agents, strategies, limit orders and automations on your machine. Signing keys stay in your operating system keychain, paper strategies keep working with no account or cloud connection, and every live trade waits for your approval in a native window that shows the exact recipient, amount, asset and chain. A tray menu lists each agent with pause, kill and review, and the mascot shows when an agent is working, waiting for you or in trouble.

entries.title: Set up your AI client with one command, and check it with doctor
entries.summary: Run npx three-ws --claude (or --cursor, --codex, --vscode, --windsurf) and the CLI signs you in, connects three.ws and verifies it, with no prompts. Keys never land in your client's config file, and running it twice changes nothing. New installers at three.ws/cli/install and three.ws/cli/claude come with a checksum and a signature so you can read and verify them before you run them. npx three-ws doctor finds a broken config, an expired sign-in or an unreachable server and tells you the fix. agent status and team show your agents, wallets and teams from the terminal.

entries.title: Sign in with Google, connect several AI clients at once, and grant permissions by group
entries.summary: You can now sign in to three.ws with Google, on the login page and on the screen an AI client sends you to when it connects. A Google account that matches an account you already verified is linked only after you confirm it on a clear page, and you can link or unlink Google any time under Settings, Sign-in methods. Connecting a second client (Claude, then ChatGPT) no longer risks the first: each client gets its own grant and both stay connected. The permissions screen groups what a client asked for into Read, Manage, Trade, Spend and Launch, says what each group can do and which actions will still ask you first, and lets you untick any group but Read before you approve. Revoking a client from Settings now stops it on its very next request, and the /connect page has the one URL and the steps for every client.

entries.title: Sign in with Telegram, link devices with one-time codes, and prove payout wallets with a signature
entries.summary: You can now sign in to three.ws with Telegram, by the login widget or by tapping a link that opens the bot. Account, Linked devices mints a short one-time code that links a phone, a desktop app, the command line (npx three-ws link) or a Telegram chat. You always see what is asking and confirm it from your signed-in browser, and you can revoke any device in one click. Agents and owners can attach a Solana or EVM wallet by signing a message. Replacing a live payout wallet now asks for your password and takes effect after a 24 hour cooldown, and every link and unlink is in your audit log. A private Telegram chat from an account you signed in with now reaches your agent without a pairing code.

entries.title: Specialist teams: four agents that research before they trade
entries.summary: Assemble a squad of four 3D agents in one click: a Researcher that vets a token and posts a scored verdict, an Entry scout that checks fresh launches against your entry gates, a Trader that quotes, simulates or trades inside one spend policy, and a Launcher that prepares a launch plan for you to sign. They share a live findings board. The Trader only acts on research it can cite, reuses a fresh verdict instead of redoing it, and every refusal is posted with its reason. Only the Trader can ever sign, and only a live trade you confirm.

entries.title: Strategies now research every coin and ask before they buy
entries.summary: Trading strategies can now check a coin before spending anything: minimum holders, how much the largest holder owns, liquidity, the rug and honeypot safety score, whether the creator can still mint or freeze, and the creator's track record. A coin that fails a check, or whose data cannot be read, is skipped and the decision log on your agent says exactly which check stopped it. You can also cap price impact per buy. Strategies now ask for your approval before each buy by default, with the amount, coin and risk notes on the card, and existing strategies were switched to ask mode too; flip one to Auto once you trust it. The strategy builder edits everything with sliders, toggles or raw JSON, turns a plain-English description into settings, shows a live count of recent launches your settings would have bought, and backtests with the checks applied.

entries.title: Talk to your squad in one sentence
entries.summary: Squad chat turns a plain sentence like "research $THREE and buy 0.05 SOL if it looks safe" into a plan of steps for your specialist team or any of your agents. Research and entry checks run live with their evidence, and anything that signs, moves funds, launches a coin or goes over your cap stops as an approval card with the full details. Approve and the squad picks the run back up and finishes with receipts. Paper mode is the default and never signs. Say "remember my default trade size is 0.1 SOL" and the squad keeps it. Coin names and descriptions are treated as data, so a coin written to trick AI agents cannot change the plan. You can type or dictate, and the squad's 3D avatars react as they work.

entries.title: The 3D agent demos show their agent again
entries.summary: Every page in the agent interaction lab had stopped drawing its 3D character, so the demos showed only text and buttons. They load again: she climbs the title, catches your cursor, rides the scroll, falls asleep on the headline and the rest. The wrecking-ball entrance was also rebuilt so she really swings in on the rope and hits the button, instead of hovering beside it with the rope pointing the wrong way.

entries.title: Token ceilings, a spend page, USDC deposits and a way out of the free tier
entries.summary: Every agent can now carry hourly, daily and per-run token ceilings next to its dollar caps. A ceiling is checked before the model is called; hitting one pauses the agent, tells you, and gives you Resume and Extend once. The new /spend page shows what each agent spends by day, by model and by tool, projects the month end, and alerts at 50, 80 and 100 percent of any cap. Credits can be topped up with USDC at a fixed rate alongside SOL and $THREE, the deposit page lists every accepted asset and its rate from live config, and paying in $THREE earns whatever bonus the owner has set. When the free tier runs out, the error now carries your choices: wait for the reset, top up, bring your own key, or resend the same request with paid_fallback: true to bill it to credits in one step.

entries.title: Your agents can trade perpetual futures
entries.summary: Each agent now has a perps desk at /agents/:id/perps, also reachable from the API and from Claude or any MCP client. It goes long or short with USDC collateral from the agent's own Solana wallet. Every agent starts in paper mode, which fills at live market prices without moving funds; live trading stays off until you turn it on for that agent. Every order is previewed with its exact margin, leverage, fees and liquidation price, runs only after you confirm, and is refused if the price moved too far in between. Leverage and per-position margin caps are always on (2x and $25 to start). A live tracker shows profit, funding paid and distance to liquidation, alerts reach you at the thresholds you set, and one kill switch closes everything.

entries.title: CAD Forge
entries.summary: Describe a mechanical part and get real parametric CAD checked by the OpenCascade kernel: STEP, STL, GLB and a drawing sheet, live dimension sliders, true-scale AR and one-click printing.

entries.title: Claim your X creations
entries.summary: Models and avatars the three.ws bot made for you on X wait here. Link the same X account and every one of them moves into your library.

entries.title: Docs · CAD Forge (text to parametric CAD)
entries.summary: How a sentence becomes a kernel-checked build123d part: the write, build and repair loop, dimension parameters, the design page, the /api/cad HTTP API, the cad_generate and cad_rebuild MCP tools, and the sandbox that runs model-written code.

entries.title: Docs · Grok Bot connector reference
entries.summary: Exact connector settings for Grok Bot, which sign-in and which server to pick, the links, jobs, retry and rate-limit contracts for unattended runs, the spend rule, and a fix for every failure the connector probe can report.

entries.title: Docs · Modly and three.ws
entries.summary: Every way three.ws works with Modly, the free open-source 3D app: generate on your own GPU from /modly or the Forge, add three.ws cloud nodes and publishing to Modly, the desktop app, and the mesh tools and slicer handoff built from Modly ideas.

entries.title: Docs · three.ws Forge for desktop
entries.summary: How to install and use three.ws Forge, the desktop 3D studio: run it from source or an installer, generate on your own GPU or the three.ws cloud, build node workflows, import CC0 models, sign in and publish to three.ws, and fix common setup problems.

entries.title: Docs · Workbench
entries.summary: How the Workbench runs a photo through an editable workflow of real GPU nodes, edits the result in the viewport, exports GLB, OBJ, STL or PLY, and how scripts call the same pipeline.

entries.title: Forge Workflows: Chain 3D Tools into One Run
entries.summary: A visual workflow builder for the Forge. Link a prompt or a photo to any live 3D engine, then remesh, rig, segment, restyle or make it game-ready, preview it inline, export the GLB and save it to your library, all in one run. Batch many prompts with ForEach, re-run from a failed step without redoing the rest, or generate on your own GPU with Modly. Starts from four templates.

entries.title: grok-skill.md
entries.summary: The three.ws skill file for Grok and Grok Bot: the connector URL to add, runnable curl calls for the free 3D studio over plain HTTPS, the links every result returns, the free limits, and the spend rule. Upload it to Grok Skills or have Grok Bot read it.

entries.title: Modly: 3D on Your Own GPU
entries.summary: Connect the free, open-source Modly app on your computer and turn an image or a prompt into a 3D model on your own graphics card. Preview it, repair or decimate the mesh, download the GLB or save it to your account. Also the hub for the Forge GPU lane, the three.ws Forge desktop app and the Modly extensions.

entries.title: The Crawl
entries.summary: Watch three.ws agents read the open web in real browsers, live. Each agent's 3D avatar walks across the page it is reading to the next link it chose, every page lands in an open corpus, and owners send their own agent out with a topic.

entries.title: three.ws Forge for Desktop
entries.summary: Download three.ws Forge, the free desktop 3D studio for Windows, Linux and Apple silicon Macs. Turn a photo into a 3D model with open-source generators on your own GPU or the three.ws cloud, chain repair, remeshing, rigging and export in node workflows, import free CC0 models and publish to your three.ws account in one click. Based on Modly (MIT).

entries.title: Tutorial · Grok Bot recipes
entries.summary: Six jobs to hand Grok Bot, each with the exact sentence, the tools it calls in order, and the real output of running that sequence against production: a daily 3D brief, a game jam asset pack, an avatar from a photo, an X post image as a 3D model, a weekly agent report and a $THREE market brief.

entries.title: Workbench
entries.summary: A desktop-style image-to-3D workspace in the browser. Drop a photo, run it through a visual workflow of real GPU nodes (background removal, mesh generation, remeshing, auto-rigging, AI material restyle), then smooth, decimate and export GLB, OBJ, STL or PLY. Build and save your own workflows in a node editor. Free, no signup.

entries.title: A build plan for the next 27 platform upgrades
entries.summary: We surveyed the strongest open-source crypto and agent projects, compared them with three.ws, and wrote the plan for closing every gap: agents that learn skills from experience, a payer command line, on-chain spending budgets, more trading venues, safer chat trading and more.

entries.title: A full setup guide for Grok Bot
entries.summary: There is now one page that covers connecting Grok Bot to three.ws end to end: the exact connector settings, which sign-in to pick, how scheduled runs collect long renders and retry without generating twice, the rate limits, the rule that an agent can never spend, and a fix for every connection problem.

entries.title: A new default engine for photo to 3D, with regional safeguards
entries.summary: Photo to 3D in the Forge now starts with TRELLIS.2, an open-source model that makes textured assets with full material detail and keeps transparency for glass and leaves. You can pick a detail level of 512, 1024 or 1536 when you generate. We also made sure that requests from the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea never use models whose license does not cover those regions, and that a request with no location signal takes the safe path too. The engine switches on as soon as its GPU worker is deployed, and until then the existing engines keep serving every request.

entries.title: A paid call that fails after payment now tells you to retry, not to pay again
entries.summary: If a paid x402 call fails after your payment has already settled, the response now says so: paid, retry safe, the settlement transaction, and how many retries are left. Repeat the exact same request with the same payment and the server re-runs the work without charging you again, instead of answering that the payment was already used. Paid POST routes also now tell apart two different request bodies sent under one payment identifier. The MCP docs gained a Use cases section that spells out every guided prompt as the ordered tool calls it makes, with the steps that spend money marked, and a test keeps it in step with the real tools.

entries.title: A skill file you can hand to Grok
entries.summary: three.ws/grok-skill.md teaches Grok and Grok Bot what three.ws does and how to use it: the one sentence that adds the free 3D connector, copy-paste commands for calling it over plain HTTPS when no connector is set up, the links every result carries, the free limits, and the rule that nothing is ever paid for without your yes.

entries.title: Agent MCP: price an x402 payment with pay_quote before pay_and_call spends it
entries.summary: The Agent MCP server now has a pay_quote tool. It asks a paid x402 endpoint what it charges without paying, and shows who gets paid, how much, in which token and on which chain, which wallet pays, the per-call limit, and anything that would stop the payment. pay_and_call needs the quote_id it returns plus an explicit confirm_payment, so an assistant always shows you the price before your agent wallet pays. One approval pays one call. Before this, turning pay_and_call on still left it refusing every call, because the quote step it requires did not exist.

entries.title: AI agents can read how to connect, per client
entries.summary: The public MCP directory at /.well-known/mcp.json now says exactly how to connect from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and Grok Bot: which server to use, which sign-in, and what to type. The /grok page is now listed in llms.txt too, so an agent can find the Grok Bot setup on its own.

entries.title: Claim the 3D models the bot made for you on X
entries.summary: Anything @trythreews makes for you from a post now waits for you. Link the same X account and every model, avatar and photo-to-3D result moves into your library, either the moment you link or from the new Claim page. If you had already linked, the bot's reply says it was saved to your library. If not, the reply carries a link to claim it.

entries.title: Cloud agents get their own free 3D budget with a connector link
entries.summary: Grok Bot and other hosted AI agents all call the free 3D studio from the same network address, so one busy user could use up the allowance for everyone. You can now mint a free, anonymous install token (on the Connect page, or with one POST) and add it to your connector link. Your agent then has its own generation budget, separate from every other installation, with no account. When any caller does hit a limit, the error now says which limit it was, when it resets, and how to raise it.

entries.title: Connect three.ws to IBM Bob
entries.summary: IBM Bob, IBM's AI development partner, is now a supported client. Open the IBM Bob tab on the connect page to copy a ready-made .bob/mcp.json entry, or run npx three-ws setup --clients bob to write it for you. The free 3D Studio server works with no account, and the connect page now fits phone screens without spilling sideways.

entries.title: Connected apps: clearer sign-in screen and instant revoke
entries.summary: When an app such as Grok Bot asks to connect to your three.ws account, the approval screen now shows the app's name and website, what it will be able to do in plain words, and says plainly that it can never spend from a wallet. The Connected apps list in Settings shows when each app was last used, and Revoke now cuts the app off on its very next request instead of waiting up to an hour for its access to run out.

entries.title: Create, Forge and Launch are easier for screen readers and AI agents to operate
entries.summary: Buttons and cards on Create and Forge now announce the same words you see on screen, the search hint and the walking companion can be reached with the keyboard, and the Launch form fields keep stable names while their character counters change.

entries.title: Creator rewards include fees pump.fun now holds on the curve and pool
entries.summary: pump.fun's October program update changed where creator rewards land: newer trades leave the creator fee on the coin's bonding curve or pool until someone sweeps it into the creator's vault. Without handling that, those rewards were invisible to a claim and read as already claimed on coin pages. Every claim on three.ws now sweeps your coins first and collects everything in the same transaction, from your wallet, an agent wallet or the automatic claimer. Reward balances, coin pages and earnings history count the held fees as unclaimed, fee-sharing changes and distributions no longer fail on unswept fees, and the biggest buy a coin ever sees (the one that completes its curve) is now reported at its full size in trade feeds and whale alerts. The automatic claimer for agent sniper wallets also had a bug that stopped every claim; that is fixed.

entries.title: Fix, smooth and slim any model in your browser, then send it straight to your 3D printer
entries.summary: Every finished model now has mesh tools: repair welds cracks and fixes inside-out faces, smoothing softens blocky surfaces without tearing textures, and decimate cuts the triangle count to a number you choose, with undo and a before and after count. Nothing is uploaded. A new 3D print action opens the model in OrcaSlicer or Bambu Studio, already upright, sized in millimetres and sitting on the build plate, with STL and 3MF downloads for every other slicer.

entries.title: Forge Workflows: chain 3D tools into one run
entries.summary: A visual workflow builder for the Forge. Link a prompt or photo to any live 3D engine, then rig, remesh, segment, restyle or make it game-ready, preview it and export or save it, all in one run. Batch many prompts or photos with For Each, re-run from a failed step without redoing the rest, or generate on your own graphics card with Modly. Starts from four ready-made templates, and the Forge page links straight to it.

entries.title: Funding an agent's inference from its wallet now needs the signed real-funds agreements
entries.summary: Topping up an agent's inference credits, switching on its automatic top-up, and provisioning an inference API key all send real USDC out of the agent's wallet. They now ask for the same signed Terms of Service, Risk Disclosure and Agent Wallet Agreement as every other real-funds action, on the page and on the API alike. Previews and switching the automatic top-up off stay open, since nothing moves.

entries.title: Generate 3D models on your own graphics card in the Forge
entries.summary: The From photos tab now has a Use your GPU panel. Install the free Modly desktop app, press Connect, and any image-to-3D model you have downloaded in Modly shows up as an engine marked Your GPU, free. Generation runs on your computer with live progress, you can cancel it at any time, and the finished model lands in the same viewer as a cloud result so you can rig it, optimize it, view it in AR, download it or save it to your avatars. Nothing on your computer is contacted until you press Connect.

entries.title: One command sets up Grok Bot
entries.summary: Run npx three-ws setup --client grok-bot to get the exact connector fields for Grok Bot, the server URL copied to your clipboard, and a live check that the public URL answers. Add --connector-key to also get a key that lets Grok Bot use your agents but never spend.

entries.title: One Grok Bot connector for 3D and your agents
entries.summary: https://three.ws/api/mcp-grok is now the one URL to paste into Grok Bot. With no sign-in it is the free 3D studio: text or an image to a 3D model, a rigged avatar, or a talking persona, with links Grok can share. Sign the same URL in with OAuth at https://three.ws/api/mcp-grok?auth=oauth, or give it an API key, and Grok also manages your agents, their memory and skills, and your avatars. It never lists a wallet, payment, card, trading or launch tool, whatever the sign-in allows, so a Grok Bot task can build with your agents but can never spend.

entries.title: Paired coins: launch a coin on Robinhood Chain that trades against up to five assets at once
entries.summary: A paired coin trades in up to five markets at the same time, each its own bonding curve: tokenized stocks, WETH, stablecoins or chain coins, in whatever split you choose. Every curve opens on a virtual reserve, so launching costs only a small flat ETH fee plus gas, and the creator never needs to hold the assets the coin pairs with. Liquidity never migrates and nobody can pull it, and the creator earns 70% of every swap fee in each asset the coin trades in, claimable in one transaction. Browse every paired coin with its pools priced in dollars, a chart per pool and every trade at /markets/robinhood/paired, and trade one from your own wallet with exact-amount approvals and slippage protection. At /launch/paired your agent launches one from its own wallet: a live quote shows each pool's opening value, the fee, gas and an optional opening buy that lands in the same transaction, and the launch runs through the agent's spend limits. Bots can do the same with two API calls, agents with the new paired-launch skill, and AI clients through the paired MCP tools. The developer guide is at /docs/paired-coins.

entries.title: pump.fun MCP tools explain the October program upgrade
entries.summary: The hosted pump.fun MCP server now tells AI clients how pump.fun's new trades change the numbers they read: a pool's virtual quote reserves are signed and often negative because fees wait in the vault until swept, a large final buy on a bonding curve finishes through a synthetic migration, and creator fees from the new trades only show up in a claim after they are swept. Graduated coins are described as moving to their PumpSwap pool, not Raydium.

entries.title: Ready-made recipes for Grok Bot and other always-on agents
entries.summary: The 3D Studio and Grok connectors now offer guided prompts written for an agent that runs on a schedule with nobody watching: a daily 3D brief that turns the top trending topic into a model and a poster image, a themed asset pack that uses the free catalog first and generates only the gaps, a rigged avatar from a photo, a quick tour, and a read-only status report on your agents. Each one names the exact tools, never stops to ask a question, and reuses a retry key so a repeated run collects the original model instead of generating twice. A new list_my_agents tool lets a signed-in connector see which agents your account holds.

entries.title: Remesh reads FBX files, and stylize says plainly when it cannot
entries.summary: The remesh tool now accepts a binary FBX for every operation, not only FBX-to-FBX conversion: convert it to GLB, OBJ or any other format, simplify it, repair it or retopologize it, even from a download link with no file extension. Stylize still cannot read FBX, so it now refuses one straight away with the formats it does take and the one-step fix (convert to GLB with remesh first), instead of accepting the job and failing later with an unexplained error. Files that cannot be read at all, such as an ASCII FBX, now fail with a message that says what to re-export. Rigged models converted to FBX also no longer carry a stray sphere mesh that the conversion used to add.

entries.title: Safe retries and live status for 3D jobs
entries.summary: The free 3D studio now has a get_job tool that reports a job's status, progress, time remaining, download links, or a failure with what to do next. Every generation tool accepts an optional idempotency_key, so a scheduled agent that retries after a timeout gets its original job back instead of starting a second one. Clients that ask for progress now receive live progress updates while a model renders.

entries.title: Six Grok Bot recipes, each run for real
entries.summary: A new tutorial gives you six jobs to hand Grok Bot: a daily 3D brief, a game jam asset pack, an avatar from a photo, an X post image turned into a 3D model, a weekly agent report and a $THREE market brief. Every one lists the exact sentence, the tools in order and the real output from a production run, and a script reruns any of them.

entries.title: Splitting a model into parts says plainly when it cannot read an FBX
entries.summary: The part splitter never could read FBX files, but it used to accept one anyway and then fail with an unexplained error. It now refuses an FBX straight away, on the website, the API and the segment_model agent tool, with the formats it does take (GLB, GLTF, OBJ, STL, PLY, OFF or DAE) and the one-step fix: convert the FBX to GLB with remesh first, then split the result. An FBX hidden behind a download link with no file extension is recognised too, and gets the same clear message instead of an error code.

entries.title: The Crawl: watch agents read the web, and send yours out
entries.summary: A new page where three.ws agents read the open web in real browsers while you watch. Each agent's own 3D avatar walks across the live page to the link it picked, says what it is thinking, then hops to the next page. Send your agent out with any topic and it reads around it until you call it home, remembering what it read so you can ask it later. Every page lands in an open corpus you can browse or download.

entries.title: The desktop companion, CLI and MCP server now work with just the bridge token
entries.summary: The companion bridge token is the one credential the desktop app, the companion command line and its MCP server are given, but the feed, marking a message as spoken, replying, reading contacts and checking sources all refused it, so pasting the token into the desktop app said it was wrong and an agent asking what you had heard got turned away. Those calls now accept the bridge token and only ever show the messages and contacts of the person it belongs to. It still cannot connect sources, edit contacts, change settings or rotate itself; those stay behind your signed-in account, and they now say so plainly instead of answering as if the token were wrong.

entries.title: The iPhone app is ready for TestFlight
entries.summary: The three.ws iPhone app now carries Apple's privacy manifests, releases to TestFlight with one command or through Xcode Cloud, and only asks for CarPlay once Apple grants it. Inside the app, buying credits, launching a coin, trading and paying now continue in Safari with one tap, still signed in and on the same page, while your wallet stays right in the app.

entries.title: The leaderboard now ranks agents by what they earned
entries.summary: A new Earned tab on the leaderboard ranks every public agent by what it earned over the last 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days or all time: creator fees from its coin plus what people and other agents paid for its skills, shown separately and added up in SOL with dollars beside it, with how far each agent moved since the previous period. Each agent's Earned card links to its place on the board, and a window you pick is saved in the page address so you can share it. The builders board also now counts launches made from an agent's own wallet, which it had been missing.

entries.title: Three ready-made jobs and the skill file on the Grok page
entries.summary: The Grok page now lists three jobs to hand Grok (an asset pack, a model with an embed, a talking persona), each naming the tools it calls, and links the Grok skill file you can upload to Grok Skills. The recent-models strip falls back to each model's concept image when a render is unavailable.

entries.title: three.ws Forge for desktop
entries.summary: A free desktop 3D studio for Windows, Linux and Apple silicon Macs, built on the open-source Modly app by Lightning Pixel. Turn a photo into a 3D model on your own graphics card or on the three.ws cloud, chain repair, remesh, rig and export steps in a node workflow, start from any model in the CC0 library, and publish to your three.ws account in one click after signing in with your browser. The download page offers the build for your system with its SHA-256, and until the first installers ship it walks you through running Forge from source.

entries.title: three.ws nodes for the Modly desktop app
entries.summary: Modly users can now add three.ws to their workflow editor. Six new nodes turn an image, a prompt or a sketch into a 3D model on our cloud GPUs, add a humanoid skeleton, rebuild the mesh as clean quads, triangles or low poly, and publish the result to a shareable three.ws page. They work on any laptop with no weights to download, and chained steps reuse the same upload instead of sending the model again. A separate Publish node saves meshes made on your own GPU to your account.

entries.title: Use three.ws from Grok Bot
entries.summary: The Connect page now has a Grok Bot tab with the exact connector settings: Streamable HTTP transport, a one-click copy of the server URL for whichever server you pick, and the right sign-in for it (none for the free servers, OAuth for the rest). Open /connect?client=grok to land on it with the Grok server already selected.

entries.title: Chart Companion
entries.summary: Paste any DEXTools pair and a 3D agent watches the live chart with you, reacting to every real swap: cheering whale buys, flinching at dumps, calling streaks and new highs, each reaction linked to its transaction. Turn on its voice, bring your own three.ws agent, embed it with one iframe, or add it to OBS as a transparent stream overlay.

entries.title: Docs · Chart Companion
entries.summary: How to watch a DEXTools chart with a 3D agent that reacts to every real swap: the URL parameters, streaming it as a transparent OBS overlay, embedding it with one iframe, bringing your own agent, and exactly how whale, streak and new-high reactions are decided.

entries.title: Docs · DEXTools integration
entries.summary: How three.ws and DEXTools connect: the /dextools hub, the embed builder that turns any DEXTools pair link into a 3D scene or Social Boost card snippet, the framable Boost on DEXTools card, and the counted redirect and public totals behind every visit three.ws sends to a DEXTools pair page.

entries.title: Docs · three.ws for Grok
entries.summary: Connect Grok Bot, Grok connectors or the xAI API to the free three.ws remote MCP server at /api/mcp-grok: text and image to 3D, rigged avatars, and a named 3D persona that lip-syncs its replies, with no account, payment or API key.

entries.title: Launch a Paired Coin
entries.summary: Have your 3D AI agent launch a coin on Robinhood Chain paired with up to five assets at once (tokenized stocks, WETH, stablecoins, chain coins) from its own wallet: a live cost quote with each pool's opening value, an atomic opening buy, spend-policy checks, and the same launch as an API call and MCP tools.

entries.title: Launch on Robinhood Chain
entries.summary: Launch a coin on Robinhood Chain through Pons, signed by your 3D AI agent's own wallet: a live cost quote, an atomic opening buy, and an API your bots can call.

entries.title: Paired Coins
entries.summary: Coins on Robinhood Chain that trade against up to five assets at once: tokenized stocks, WETH, stablecoins and chain coins, each in its own bonding curve with liquidity locked forever. Live pools priced in dollars, charts per pool, every trade, a buy and sell ticket, and the AI agents that launched them.

entries.title: three.ws for Grok
entries.summary: One sentence gives Grok Bot a 3D studio. Text and images become textured 3D models, rigged avatars, and a talking 3D body Grok can wear. Works in Grok Bot, Grok connectors and the xAI API. Free, no account, no key.

entries.title: three.ws x DEXTools
entries.summary: Every way three.ws works with DEXTools: DEXTools charts in every coin chart, any DEXTools pair rendered as a live 3D scene, a Social Boost card any project can embed, and a public count of the visits three.ws sends to DEXTools pair pages. Paste a DEXTools link to get the embed snippet.

entries.title: 3D Studio results now hand every agent plain links to the model
entries.summary: Every model the free 3D Studio MCP server hands back, whether freshly generated, picked from the asset catalog or saved as a persona, now comes with four plain links, both in the result data and in its first lines of text: a viewer page, the GLB file, a rendered PNG picture and a paste-ready embed snippet. Agents that cannot show a 3D widget, like Grok Bot and other browser agents, can now open, download, share and embed the model directly. A model that is still rendering comes with a viewer link that waits for the job and opens the model the moment it is ready.

entries.title: Agent earnings are updating again
entries.summary: pump.fun moved the service that reports creator fees, so the Earned figures on agent pages, agent profiles, coin pages and /analytics had stopped refreshing since the end of September. Earnings now read from pump.fun's current fees service, with a second source behind it if that one stumbles, and every agent coin is back on its 30-minute refresh.

entries.title: Chart Companion: a 3D agent that watches the chart with you
entries.summary: Paste any DEXTools pair at /chart-companion and a 3D agent sits beside the live chart, reacting to every real swap as it lands: a superhero jump for a whale buy, a facepalm for a dump, a dance for a buy streak, applause for a new daily high. Each reaction comes with a line you can trace to its transaction, and it can read them aloud. Bring your own three.ws agent, embed it on your coin's site with one iframe, or add it to OBS as a transparent overlay for your stream.

entries.title: Chat and agents stay up through more AI outages
entries.summary: Every AI answer on three.ws, from chat to agent brains, the tutor and the fact-checker, now has five more free models to fall back on when the usual ones are busy. NVIDIA's largest open model, Nemotron 3 Ultra, now answers right behind Nemotron 3 Super, with the compact Nemotron 3.5 Lightning further down the line. A second, independent route to the same Nemotron models works with no account at all, and a Gemma 4 model is back in the mix as well. The free NVIDIA and gateway models are now checked against their providers every six hours too, so the team hears the moment one is switched off instead of finding out from a failed answer.

entries.title: Coin charts say plainly when a coin has no market yet
entries.summary: A coin with no trading pool anywhere could show a price-history error on its chart when a market data source was busy. The chart now recognises the coin has no market and shows the no-price-history state, and it asks that source one question fewer per chart load.

entries.title: Coin Clash stays playable when community data is offline
entries.summary: When the community roster behind Coin Clash is unavailable, the arena no longer goes dark. Each round is now fought between the coins trending on Solana right now, locked in for the whole round so battles never reshuffle mid-fight, and each army shows its market cap where the member count would be. Enlisting, rallying and war records work exactly as before.

entries.title: Coin pages keep their Markets table when the listing sources are busy
entries.summary: When both of our exchange-listing sources were rate-limited, a coin page's Markets table could show an error for coins only one of them lists. It now falls back to the coin's live DEX trading pairs, found by its contract address, with each pair's venue, chain, price, 24h volume and a link to trade it.

entries.title: Community sentiment readings are back on coin pages and the Oracle
entries.summary: pump.fun moved the feed of community callouts that our sentiment pulse reads, so every reading had been failing with an unavailable error. The pulse now reads the new feed, so launch pages, the Oracle and the sentiment_pulse MCP tool score real community commentary again, up to 100 callouts per coin.

entries.title: DEXTools is one click away on every coin, and every visit counts toward Social Boost
entries.summary: DEXTools Social Boost ranks tokens by visits to their DEXTools page, and $THREE has already won three buybacks from it. Every coin on three.ws now carries a DEXTools link: it leads the trading terminal row and appears on coin and launch pages, the 3D coin view, the Oracle, agent and character pages, the live pump.fun feeds and your token dashboard. Each link opens the coin's busiest pair on DEXTools, so the visit lands on the page Social Boost actually counts. Launch pages, and the success screen right after you launch a coin, also get a Social Boost card that explains how the ranking works and sends your community there in one click. Visits are counted in daily totals per coin and per page that sent them. No visitor data is stored.

entries.title: Event-attested reputation now requires the platform's own signature
entries.summary: The event-attested tier in a Solana agent's reputation, which ranks above community feedback in the Passport grade, was granted on a label written inside the memo, so any signer could claim it. It now counts only attestations the platform's own attester minted and recorded, so a self-written label earns ordinary feedback weight and nothing more.

entries.title: Fewer failed 3D generations when the concept image comes back blank
entries.summary: Text to 3D first paints a concept image, then sculpts it. When the painting service quietly returned a blank black frame instead of a picture, the studio used it anyway, and every 3D engine then failed because there was nothing in the image to sculpt. The studio now spots a blank or withheld frame and paints the concept with the next image service instead, so those prompts finish as real models.

entries.title: Grok model menus now offer xAI's current models
entries.summary: Every Grok picker on three.ws (the /brain menu, agent chat, the avatar page and the embed editor) now lists xAI's current line-up: Grok 4.7, xAI's flagship, Grok 4.3 with its 1M-token context at the lowest Grok price, Grok 4.20 Fast with no thinking pass, and Grok Build for coding. Agents and embeds that saved a Grok model xAI has since retired, such as Grok 4.1 Fast, keep working and answer on the model xAI recommends in its place. People who bring their own xAI key now get Grok 4.7 by default instead of an older flagship.

entries.title: Picking the free Hugging Face engine no longer leaves you stuck when its Spaces are down
entries.summary: When every free Hugging Face Space is out of GPU quota, the Forge now pauses that engine for a few minutes, greys it out in the engine picker with the reason, and moves a generation you started on it to a working engine, showing you the switch, instead of retrying the same dead Spaces with a countdown.

entries.title: Shared 3D models now explain themselves to X and Grok
entries.summary: Every 3D model page now tells whoever reads the link exactly what it is. A model shared from three.ws unfurls on X as a large card showing a render of the model itself instead of a stock image, with its own title and description. Model, avatar and agent pages also describe themselves in a machine-readable form that search engines and AI assistants like Grok can read: the 3D file, a picture of it, who made it, when, and the terms it is shared under. So when someone asks Grok what a three.ws link is, it can answer from the model rather than guess.

entries.title: Signing in to the 3D Studio, wallet, Bazaar and IBM MCP servers works from any connector
entries.summary: Adding the 3D Studio, agent wallet, x402 Bazaar or IBM Granite MCP server to an AI client with sign-in (Grok Bot, claude.ai connectors and any client built on the official MCP SDK) used to stop before the consent screen, because every server pointed the client at sign-in details written for the core server only. Each server now describes itself and issues a sign-in bound to it, so the connector reaches consent, gets its token and connects. Existing connections keep working. The MCP docs now carry a compatibility table with the exact connector settings for every server, and `npm run probe:mcp-clients` checks all of them the way a cloud client connects.

entries.title: The coin visualizer and communities keep loading when pump.fun throttles us
entries.summary: The full coin board behind the pump.fun visualizer, the communities page and the home page's live coin now retries a rate-limited read once and falls back to the last board any server saw in the past 30 minutes, marked as slightly stale, instead of showing an error.

entries.title: Your agent can launch its own coin on Robinhood Chain
entries.summary: Agents can now launch a coin on Robinhood Chain through Pons, the chain's busiest launchpad, signed by the agent's own wallet. Name the coin, see the exact cost live (launch fee, opening buy, gas, and how many tokens the opening buy gets), confirm, and it is trading on a bonding curve in about a second. The opening buy lands in the same transaction, so nobody trades ahead of your agent. Bots can do the same through two API calls or the new pons-launch skill, and launched coins show up on /launches and the agent's profile. The Recent Launches feed on /markets/robinhood now lists every Pons launch too, with curve price, market cap and graduation progress.

entries.title: Avatar pictures show a natural standing pose instead of a T-pose
entries.summary: The small pictures of avatars around the site, on Spotlight cards, in the Monitor fleet list, on Characters and on the Rankings board, were drawn with every avatar standing arms out in a stiff T. Avatar pictures are now drawn with the avatar standing naturally, arms relaxed at its sides, using the same posing the live 3D viewer uses, and that works for every skeleton style the viewer already understands. Props, vehicles and creatures are drawn exactly as they were made. Avatar pictures also keep their colored backdrop and their real textures again, where some had come out on plain black with bare white materials. Every avatar picture drawn from now on uses the new pose, and the older pictures can now be redrawn in place.

entries.title: Avatars no longer open in a T-pose, and Spotlight shows one avatar instead of two
entries.summary: On an Agent Spotlight page the avatar's preview picture, which is rendered arms out, never went away once the live 3D avatar loaded, so a second, T-posed copy stood behind the real one for as long as the page was open. The picture now gives way the moment the live avatar is ready. Separately, every embedded 3D avatar briefly showed its arms-out rest pose while its idle animation loaded and then faded in from it. The avatar now stays hidden until it is standing in its idle, then fades in, everywhere the avatar component is used.

entries.title: Pinned agent-3d embeds keep working after every update
entries.summary: If you embedded the 3D avatar component with a pinned version and an integrity hash, as our docs recommend for production, the embed could stop loading after one of our updates: the file behind a version that is promised never to change was being rebuilt each time we shipped, so its fingerprint changed and browsers refused to run it. A released version is now frozen for good, every update serves exactly the same file under it, and the build fails if any hash in our docs, skills or code snippets ever disagrees with the file it points to. Version 1.5.2 is frozen as it is served today; if your page pins an older hash for 1.5.2, update it once from /agent-3d/1.5.2/integrity.json.
